arms.better: tm located the exact transform and relevant stream tests quickly and recovered from several failed tool calls, but the progress feed hid useful test detail behind the generic “Ran tests” message. Its repeated submit/save errors (“couldn't find that,” “hit an unexpected internal problem,” and “got a response it couldn't understand”) gave no actionable recovery information. The focused hidden stream tests pass, but the prescribed full test command did not: pnpm rejected ignored dependency build scripts, npm test stopped on an existing lint error, and browser tests could not launch Firefox/WebKit because those browsers are not installed. A concise final report that names the exact verification command/results, paired with more specific errors and retry guidance, would improve confidence and usability. The reported tm stats usage was 462,517 input tokens and zero output tokens; this unusually high input count is recorded as emitted by tm stats.

OpenCode made a reasonable scoped edit and reported the focused-test failure honestly, but it spent multiple iterations modifying streamResponse and its temporary regression test without understanding that the issue’s empty-body stream reaches the TransformStream flush path. The temporary test itself exercised a null response body rather than the reported empty stream body, so it led the investigation away from the issue. The official hidden stream tests passed after their files were restored, including empty response completion, but the required whole-suite verification did not pass because of the environment’s dependency-build policy, a pre-existing lint error, and unavailable Firefox/WebKit binaries. A closer initial read of the request/response stream lifecycle and use of the repository’s canonical regression-test shape would reduce the rework.
